Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tna 1.5.8

  • permutation_test(): comparing two models with scaled edge weights gives a message (class tna_message_scaling). Each network is scaled on its own, so comparing scaled weights is not warranted; the test still runs.

tna 1.5.7

  • estimate_cs(): the CS-coefficient is the largest passing proportion, whatever the order of drop_prop.
  • permutation_test(): adjust corrects over the edges tested (present in either network), not every cell.

tna 1.5.6

  • group_model(), group_tna(), group_ftna() and group_ctna(): window parameters in params and windows recorded by import_onehot() had no effect, so a grouped model of the same call as tna() gave different weights. They are now used, as in build_model().

tna 1.5.5

  • NEWS.md wording.

tna 1.5.4

Corrections to numerical results. Results from the functions below can differ from earlier versions.

  • bootstrap_cliques() resampled from the first sequences only, as many as there were cliques (for example, 22 of 2,000 sequences), so its p-values and confidence intervals were invalid. Each bootstrap sample now draws as many sequences as the data has.
  • reliability() counted the transitions of the model it was given for every requested type, so types only switched the row normalization on or off: "co-occurrence", "gap", "attention", and the other types all gave the frequency result. Each type is now estimated as build_model() defines it. The default types is the type of the model (it was "relative" for every model).
  • compare(): the Canberra distance omitted the edges present in only one network (each contributes 1), and the distance correlation was reported squared. The states of the two networks are matched by name, so two networks listing the same states in a different order are compared correctly; networks with different states, or a matrix without state names, are an error of class tna_error_states (they were compared by position).
  • summary() of a model reported the standard deviation of the in-strength as that of the out-strength and vice versa (the means are equal by construction).
  • estimate_cs(): a subsample in which the correlation is undefined (the measure is constant in it) was dropped from the share of draws above threshold, which could raise the CS-coefficient. It now counts as a draw below the threshold.
  • BetweennessRSP counted the correction for walks absorbed at a target once for every state, also for states that cannot reach it. In a network that is not strongly connected (for example, with a state that is never entered) the values were wrong. Only sources that reach the target are counted; strongly connected networks are unchanged.
  • simulate(): zero_row was replaced by the value of format, so zero_row = "uniform" had no effect for frequency models, and states that are never left (such as a state that only ends sequences) moved arbitrarily in relative models. zero_row now applies to both model types. max_len = 1 and na_range values with equal ends or a zero lower end no longer fail.
  • prune(method = "disparity") set the absent edges of a state with no outgoing or no incoming edges to NA. They stay 0.
  • build_model() of a wide data.frame discarded window_size, window_span, and windowed given in params. They are now used.
  • Backward (and bidirectional) attention paired every time point with itself, adding a self-loop of full weight at every observation. Only earlier time points are attended to, as forward attention uses only later ones.
  • group_model() kept the unused factor levels of group, so a level with no sequences became an empty network with NaN initial probabilities. Unused levels are dropped.
  • print() of a model without initial probabilities (for example, build_model() of a matrix) failed. plot() of a model failed when node_size or vsize was given, and plot_sequences(show_n = FALSE) failed.
  • permutation_test() and estimate_cs() took the observed network from the weights of the model but rebuilt the resamples from the sequence data, so a pruned model was compared with unpruned resamples (a model tested against its own pruned version showed significant differences). The observed network is now rebuilt from the sequence data too, as in bootstrap(). Results for unpruned models are unchanged.
  • end_state was not added when no sequence filled the last column of the data (for example, in a subset of the rows, or with an empty trailing column). It is now always added after the last observation.
  • build_model() of a tsn object ordered the time points by first appearance in the data, not by time, which could reverse transitions. They are now ordered by time.
  • cliques(sum_weights = TRUE) applied threshold to each direction before summing them, so a pair whose summed weight exceeded the threshold could be missed. The threshold now applies to the sum, as documented. This also affects bootstrap_cliques() with a positive threshold.
  • import_onehot(window_type = "sliding") widened the windows of width 3 or more (each lag was applied to the already widened rows), and treated width 1 as width 2. Each window now covers exactly window_size rows, and the incomplete windows at the start are dropped. Width 2 is unchanged.
  • plot_associations() drew every residual in the reverse direction (from target to source).
  • plot() of grouped communities colored every state of a group with the same color. Each community now has its own color, as for a single group.

tna 1.5.3

  • Documentation revision. The help pages describe what the functions return as they do now: summary() of a model (a table of 13 metrics, not a list), communities(), cliques(), compare(), compare_sequences() (the default sub is 1:5), permutation_test(), bootstrap() (with its model element), reliability(), prepare_data(), import_data(), import_onehot(), simulate(), plot_compare(), and pruning_details(). The default of na.rm in group_model() is TRUE, as in the code, and a missing group is an error. prune() documents its four methods, including that only "threshold" and "lowest" keep the network weakly connected, and reprune() has its own help page.
  • Examples no longer reach into result objects with $ or subset the data with brackets; print(<tna_data>) examples use the data argument (they used which, which was ignored). centralities(), prune(), and cluster_sequences() cite the methods they implement.
  • Vignettes and articles: the tables of the getting-started vignette, the grouped-sequences vignette, and the README use print() and summary() instead of $weights, $inits, and $centralities$stats; the clusters are built with group_tna(<clustering>); bootstrap() calls no longer pass a threshold that the default method ignores; the time threshold of prepare_data() is in seconds; the frequency and attention articles restore their options(), and the frequency article compares the scaled weights with compare().

tna 1.5.2

  • summary() of a permutation test returns the centrality results with what = "centralities" (the edges remain the default).
  • New summary() method for reliability() results: all 22 split-half metrics, with their category, as a tidy table (print() shows four).
  • New article “Validating a transition network” covering markov_order(), bootstrap() and bootstrap pruning, estimate_cs(), reliability(), permutation_test() (including edge betweenness), compare_sequences(), and the actor argument for nested data.
  • Every vignette and article ends with a list of the package articles, the TNA tutorials and book chapters, and the Dynalytics resources (package sites, tools, CarmNotes, and selected articles).

tna 1.5.1

  • Small examples on a subset of the data come before the \donttest{} blocks of compare_sequences(), estimate_cs(), plot_frequencies() for groups, and the print, plot and summary methods of sequence comparisons and stability results. The as.igraph() methods have examples.
  • permutation_test() for groups and the plot() methods of bootstrap and reliability results document what they return.
  • The vignette “A showcase of the main tna functions” restores the options() it changes.
  • The plots of the README are no longer part of the package, which reduces the installed size from 6.3 to 4.1 MB.

tna 1.5.0

  • compare_sequences() now rejects arguments it does not use. A misspelled argument such as correction = "fdr" (the argument is adjust) was silently ignored and the default Bonferroni correction applied; the vignette on grouped sequences had this mistake and now uses adjust = "fdr" as its text describes.

  • Fixed build_model() and group_model() for data with a single time point: the sequences were joined into one row, which created transitions that do not exist (and group_model() failed).

  • Fixed group_model() and group_tna() with a character group: when the data did not start with the alphabetically first group, every network was labelled with another group’s name. Groups keep their order of first appearance and now hold their own sequences.

  • Fixed scaling across groups (groupwise = FALSE, the default) dropping the state names of the weight matrices, which made communities() and compare() fail.

  • Fixed centralities() naming the states 1, 2, … instead of their labels when the only measures requested were Diffusion or BetweennessRSP (whose computations return unnamed values); the centrality table of permutation_test(measures = "Diffusion") had the same problem.

  • New summary() methods for tna_permutation, group_tna_permutation, tna_stability, and group_tna_stability objects return tidy tables: one row per edge (from, to, diff_true, effect_size, p_value) and one row per measure (measure, cs_coefficient).

  • Permutation effect sizes are NA where the permuted differences do not vary, instead of Inf or NaN (permutation_test() for edges and centralities, and compare_sequences()). Whether they vary is judged against the magnitude of the compared values, so the rule does not depend on the measurement scale.

  • Grouped models with scaled edge weights (group_model(scaling = ), with either value of groupwise) and the networks they contain are no longer resampled: bootstrap(), bootstrap_cliques(), permutation_test(), estimate_cs(), reliability(), and compare_sequences() raise an error of class tna_error_scaling. Scaling across groups depends on every group, so a resample of one group cannot reproduce it. Before, bootstrap() and permutation_test() refused such a group as a whole, but estimate_cs() on the group, and every resampling function on one of its networks (for example bootstrap(model[[1]])), rebuilt the resamples without the scaling and compared them with the scaled network. Resampling of single scaled models (tna(x, scaling = )) is unchanged.

  • Fixed centralities(measures = "BetweennessRSP") returning a single row for a network with a state that has no outgoing transitions; BetweennessRSP is NA for every state there.

  • summary() of an estimate_cs() result keeps its columns when nothing could be estimated, and a grouped summary no longer fails when one group has no results.

  • New markov_order() tests whether sequences are described by a first-order Markov chain, the assumption of a transition network, or depend on states further back. Each order is tested against the order below with the likelihood-ratio statistic (Anderson & Goodman, 1957) and a conditional permutation test that shuffles the next states within each context. The orders are tested in sequence, and the results also report the log-likelihood, AIC, and BIC of the multi-order model of each order (Scholtes, 2017). Methods for tna and group_tna objects, with print(), summary(), and plot() methods. plot() draws two panels: the log-likelihood, AIC, and BIC across the orders with the selected order marked, and the permutation null density of each order with the observed statistic (panel = "ic" or "permutation" draws one; unknown arguments are errors). Because the tests stop at the first order that does not reject, a dependence that skips an order is not selected: a warning of class tna_warning_markov_order and a printed note flag a higher order whose test rejects and AIC or BIC choosing another order. The same warning is raised when iter is too small for any p-value to fall below level.

  • estimate_cs() gains the argument edges: with edges = TRUE, the stability of the edge weights is estimated alongside the centralities and returned as the element Edges. Only the edges present in the network are compared, because an edge absent from the data cannot appear in a subsample and would only add agreeing zeros.

  • Diffusion centrality is now always normalized to the range from 0 to 1 (min-max), whatever the value of normalize, in centralities() and in everything that uses it (permutation_test(measures = ), compare(), estimate_cs(), plots). Its raw values grow with powers of the edge weights and exceed 1e30 for frequency models. Where diffusion does not vary across the states (a relative model with loops = TRUE), it is NaN.

  • Fixed resampling of edge betweenness networks. The resampling functions rebuilt a model from betweenness_network() with all weights equal to zero, so permutation_test() gave the smallest possible p-value and an infinite effect size to every edge whose betweenness differed, bootstrap() returned no edges, every CS-coefficient of estimate_cs() was 0, and reliability() compared empty networks. betweenness_network() now records the model it was built from. In permutation_test(), bootstrap(), and estimate_cs(), every resample rebuilds that model and recomputes edge betweenness, so permutation_test() on two edge betweenness networks tests their differences in edge betweenness; reliability() uses the transitions of that model. betweenness_network() also has a method for group_tna objects, so permutation_test(betweenness_network(models)) compares edge betweenness between all groups in one call.

    Edge betweenness networks created by earlier versions must be rebuilt to be resampled, and betweenness_network() refuses a network that is already an edge betweenness network.

tna 1.4.0

  • New actor argument for sequences nested in actors (for example, several sessions per student) in every resampling method: permutation_test(), bootstrap(), estimate_cs(), reliability(), compare_sequences(), and prune(method = "bootstrap") through bootstrap(). actor is a column name of the data the model was built from, or a vector with one identifier per sequence. With one sequence per actor, every method gives the same result as without actor.
    • Permutation tests reassign whole actors between groups and shuffle the sequences of actors present in several groups within the actor (Good, 2005). A warning is given when the actors allow too few distinct permutations to reach the significance level.
    • Bootstraps resample whole actors with replacement (cluster bootstrap; Davison & Hinkley, 1997).
    • Case-dropping (estimate_cs()) drops whole actors, and split-half reliability puts all sequences of an actor in the same half.
  • Models keep the non-sequence columns of their data (one row per sequence), so actor can name any of them. This includes models built from prepare_data() output, grouped models, and cluster_data() of prepare_data() output. With concat > 1, the columns that are constant within each concatenated block are kept. Grouped models record the rows of each group, so an actor vector for the full data applies to every group, including groups from mixture models.

tna 1.3.1

CRAN release: 2026-09-28

  • Fixed prepare_data() emitting a dplyr grouping message when computing sessions per user; the summarise now drops its grouping explicitly.

tna 1.3.0

  • Fixed case-insensitive argument matching to preserve canonical option names, allowing cluster_data() and cluster_sequences() to pass "ward.D" and "ward.D2" correctly to stats::hclust().
  • Made state ordering deterministic across system locales for individual and grouped models.
  • Fixed numerical instability in randomized-shortest-path betweenness and prevented normalization from amplifying floating-point noise in constant centrality measures.
  • Added deterministic timezone handling to prepare_data(): UTC is the default, explicit offsets are honored, fractional seconds are retained, and offset-free timestamps can use a user-specified Olson timezone.
  • prepare_data(time_threshold = FALSE) now disables gap-based session splitting while retaining timestamp parsing and event ordering.
  • prepare_data() now supports explicit session columns and collision-safe composite actor/session identities, including high-cardinality groupings. Disabled time splitting now bypasses gap computation and keeps missing-time events in their actor-session sequence.
  • Documented the time_data component returned by prepare_data().
  • prune() now warns about inactive method-specific arguments and treats a supplied bootstrap object as a request for bootstrap pruning.
  • Added reproducible seed arguments to network and clique bootstrapping.
  • Added weighted PageRank to centralities().
  • plot.tna_permutation() now dispatches to the dedicated permutation renderer of cograph::splot(), so permutation-specific options such as show_nonsig, show_stars, show_effect, edge_nonsig_color, edge_nonsig_style, and edge_nonsig_alpha are honored.
  • Fixed qgraph-style plotting arguments (such as edge.label.cex) being ignored by matrix-based network plots (e.g. permutation and disparity plots).
  • Added a bins argument to plot.tna_reliability() for controlling the number of histogram bins.

tna 1.2.3

CRAN release: 2026-04-26

  • Resolved CRAN warning “Data files with namespace references not in the recursive strong package dependencies” by rebuilding engagement_mmm as a tna_mmm object that carries no foreign class references. The new sibling S3 methods group_model.tna_mmm() and mmm_stats.tna_mmm() preserve all existing example behaviour without requiring seqHMM at example-run time. Real mhmm objects from seqHMM continue to work via the original *.mhmm methods.
  • Added random_tna(), random_group_tna(), random_tna_mmm(), and list_random_state_pools() for constructing synthetic TNA models with no external dependencies.
  • Lowered the minimum required R version from 4.4.0 to 4.1.0 (the floor set by the native |> pipe used in the package).

tna 1.2.2

CRAN release: 2026-04-15

  • Fix bug in plot.tna_sequence_comparison

tna 1.2.1

  • The test argument of compare_sequences() is now TRUE by default for backward compatibility.
  • Fixed an issue with bootstrap() when the model contained weights that were zero.
  • Fixed issues with several distance measures in cluster_sequences().
  • Fixed edge ordering in betweenness_network().
  • The packages no longer depends on qgraph.
  • Network plotting functionality now relies on cograph instead.

tna 1.2.0

CRAN release: 2026-02-12

  • Added the function reliability() for reliability analysis of tna models.
  • The import_onehot() function has been redesigned with new features.
  • Replaced the Z tests and chi-squared tests in compare_sequences() with a permutation test.
  • Removed the chi-squared test from plot_mosaic().
  • The correct argument of compare_sequences() has been renamed to adjust to align with other similar arguments.
  • Added several new arguments to the plot method of tna objects for plotting heterogeneous networks.
  • The plot method for communities now uses the first available method by default.
  • The stringdist package has been moved to Suggests.
  • Added additional checks for missing columns when using tidy selections in various functions that were previously silently ignored.

tna 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2025-10-18

  • Added the function cluster_sequences() to cluster sequence data using string distance measures of the stringdist package.
  • Added the function compare_sequences() to compare the frequencies of patterns between groups for sequence data.
  • prepare_data() now accepts a character vector for the actor argument.

tna 1.0.0

CRAN release: 2025-07-15

  • CRAN release

tna 0.7.0

  • Added the function import_onehot() to read one-hot data.
  • The function plot_sequences() gains the argument ncol for selecting the number of columns of the facets.

tna 0.6.1

  • The group column is now automatically removed from cols in group_model().

tna 0.6.0

  • Added a new method plot_sequences() for sequence index plots and state distribution plots.

tna 0.5.1

  • Fixed the handling of missing values in group_model() with stslist objects.
  • Fixed an issue with plot.group_tna_permutation() that resulted in plotting arguments not being passed to qgraph.

tna 0.5.0

CRAN release: 2025-05-26

  • Added a new dataset group_regulation_long.

tna 0.4.9

  • Switched to matrix as the internal data format used by TNA models for performance improvements across all functions.

tna 0.4.8

  • Fixed an issue with prepare_data() that resulted in excessive console output.

tna 0.4.7

  • Added the function import_data() to read wide format sequence data into long format.

tna 0.4.6

  • Added the function plot_frequencies() that can be used to plot the state frequency distribution for both tna and group_tna objects.

tna 0.4.5

  • The function permutation_test() is now a method for both ungrouped (build_model()) and grouped (group_model()) models. For grouped models, the function performs the test between every unique pair of groups.
  • A new argument adjust has been added for permutation_test() to optionally adjust p-values using p.adjust. By default, the p-values are not adjusted (adjust = "none").
  • A new argument groupwise has been added for group_model(). When FALSE (the default), scaling methods listed in scaling are performed globally over the groups. When TRUE, the scaling is performed within each group instead (this was the default behavior in previous versions of the package).
  • Added a simulate() method for tna objects. For models with type = "relative", this function simulates sequence data based on the initial probabilities and transition probability matrix.

tna 0.4.4

  • The plot.tna_centralities() and plot.group_tna_centralities() functions now plot the centralities in the same order as provided in the measures argument.
  • The plot.tna() and plot_model() functions now use the median edge weight as the default value for the cut argument.
  • Fixed the from and to columns in bootstrap() output, which were inverted from the true edge direction.
  • A plot method has been added for the bootstrap() output, which plots the corresponding network where non-significant edges have been pruned.

tna 0.4.3

  • The permutation_test() function now properly checks that its arguments x and y can be compared.
  • The p-value calculations of permutation_test() and bootstrap() have been adjusted by adding 1 to both the number of permutations/bootstrap samples and the number of extreme events so that these estimates are never zero. The documentation has also been clarified regarding p-values emphasizing that these are estimates only.

tna 0.4.2

  • The plot_compare() function now supports negCol and posCol for specifying the color of the positive and negative differences in transition and initial probabilities.
  • The plot_mosaic() function now plots the x-axis on the top and rotates the labels 90 degrees only when there are more than three groups.

tna 0.4.1

  • The detailed argument of estimate_centrality_stability() has been removed. Previously this argument had no effect on the output of the function.
  • Removed several duplicated entries in the documentation.

tna 0.4.0

CRAN release: 2025-03-01

  • The prepare_data() function now produces an object of class tna_data, which can be directly used as an argument to build_model() and other methods.
  • The prepare_data() function now supports order when used together with time and actor.
  • The prepare_data() function gains the unused_fn argument of tidyr::pivot_wider() to process any extra columns. The default is to keep all columns and use the first value.
  • Added the function compare() to compare tna models and weight matrices. This function produces an object of class tna_comparison which has print() and plot() methods.
  • Added the function plot_mosaic() which can be used to produce mosaic plots of transition counts for frequency-based transition network models and to contrast the state counts between groups.
  • Fixed an issue with plot.tna_communities() which now checks for the availability of a particular community detection method before plotting.
  • Made several arguments in the plot methods of the package accessible to the user.

tna 0.3.2

  • event2sequence() has been renamed to prepare_data(). The function is now also more general and can process more date formats.
  • Added a method argument to bootstrap(). The new default option "stability" implements a bootstrapping scheme where the edge weights are compared against a range of “consistent” weights (see the documentation for details). The old functionality can be accessed with method = "threshold".
  • Fixed an issue with permutatation_test() when x and y had a differing number of columns.
  • Community detection methods can now be selected using the methods argument in communities().
  • The build_model() function has gained the argument cols which can be used to subset the columns of the data for stslist and data.frame inputs.
  • Removed all verbose arguments in favor of options(rlib_message_verbosity = "quiet"). and options(rlib_warning_verbosity = "quiet").

tna 0.3.1

  • Fixed an issue when checking the validity of character type arguments.
  • Improved the bootstrap() function to determine edge significance based on deviation from the observed value, rather than a fixed threshold.
  • Added a helper function event2sequence() to parse event data into sequence data.

tna 0.3.0

CRAN release: 2024-12-11

  • Added support for grouped sequence data (clusters).

tna 0.2.0

  • Added bootstrapping, permutation test, and centrality stability functionalities.

tna 0.1.0

  • Initial version.
